reason: E2 shows W addition raises crystallization temperatures in Fe-based amorphous alloys due to strong W-P bonding, supporting the thermal stability premise. E1 demonstrates W-containing metallic glasses with good thermal stability, but uses mechanical alloying, not rapid quenching, so it only loosely supports the amorphous retention and processing condition premises. The atomic size mismatch and viscosity premises are not directly evidenced by the cited passages.
premises: W addition increases atomic size mismatch and melt viscosity
W forms strong exothermic bonds with P, increasing cohesive energy
Increased viscosity and cohesive energy suppress crystallization kinetics
W addition improves thermal stability and amorphous retention in metallic glasses
The effect is specific to rapid quenching and moderate reheating conditions
